newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on weather, demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on weather, demand.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended higher Monday in response to concern over the U.S. crop's ability to withstand very cold weather in the Southern Plains, traders said.
"There is some worry about the weather, but I think the crop will end up being okay when all is said and done," said one wheat trader.

Hard red winter wheat growing areas had unseasonably warm temperatures over the weekend. That weather was said to melt the crop's insulating snow cover and leave it more vulnerable to damage from winterkill, traders said.
Advances were pared by a late sell-off in the soybean pit, traders said.
The market also derived some demand-related support from news that the U.S. Treasury Department granted Cargill permission to sell up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat and rice.
However, bearish traders said wheat for that deal could be sourced from any country,
"Just because it is a U.S. company doesn't mean it's going to be U.S. wheat," a trader said.
CBOT wheat futures ended two to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-1/2 at $3.88-1/2.
Ongoing demand for wheat from Bangladesh, South Korea, Egypt and Slovenia also helped underpin futures, traders said.
U.S. Department of Agriculture export shipments of 11.5 million bushels also prompted some buying during the session, traders said.
The inspections came in at the high end of trade expectations for six to 12 million bushels, floor sources said.
On the day, Produce Grain sold one million bushels March, Iowa Grain bought one million March, and Paine Webber bought one million March.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 9,077 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
